title: Investigate deferred-free lag and page staleness in KV prefetching under mixed-sequence continuous batching
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Symptom: Over the last two weeks we intermittently observe slowly increasing GPU resident page counts and repeated small OOM spikes on heavy KV-prefetch workloads using continuous batching. This occurs only when the request mix contains a long tail of very short and very long sequences (e.g., 8-token chat messages mixed with 2048-token generation) and when KV prefetch is enabled with aggressive concurrency.

Observed behavior:
- GPU resident bytes trend upward across many hours without corresponding increase in active batch token throughput.
- Periodic latency spikes align with small increases in device-resident page counts.
- nvprof / nsight sampling shows many pending cudaFree/async-free operations on non-default streams and delayed decommit of staging buffers.
- cuMemPool/allocator counters indicate backlog in deferred free queues and high fragmentation in small-slab pools.

Hypothesis: cudaMallocAsync's deferred free path is interacting poorly with our KV prefetch and multi-stream continuous-batch merge logic. Two contributing mechanisms suspected: (1) prefetch spawns eviction/fill work on auxiliary streams that leave pinned or staged buffers referenced across streams, preventing immediate release to the memory pool; (2) mixed-sequence batching causes merged batches to briefly hold references to older KV slices, increasing allocation churn and fragmenting small-slab pools. The allocator's deferred-free queue therefore accumulates resident pages until epoch compaction runs, producing a slow-residence drift.

Why this is critical: Regressions can cause predictable degradation for tail-latency-sensitive customers and make Dedicated capacity utilization inefficient (higher reserved memory and worse packing).

Repro steps (dev repro harness):
1) Run reuseable continuous-batching harness on a single A100-40GB instance with workload mix: 70% short (seq=8), 20% medium (seq=128), 10% long (seq=2048).
2) Enable KV prefetch with prefetch_concurrency=8 and eviction_threshold=0.6.
3) Run for 4+ hours and monitor cuMemPool statistics, cudaMemGetInfo, and our internal allocator metrics.
4) Trigger compaction and observe drop in resident pages; measure time between compaction runs.

Diagnostics already collected:
- Profiling tarball: https://storage.redwood.ai/artifacts/ENG-31500/profiles/2026-03-02.tar.gz
- Grafana panel (allocator / resident pages): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocator/residency?orgId=1&panelId=45
- Repro harness: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/tree/eng/mem-harness (branch: ENG-31500-repro)
- Initial PR with extended allocator metrics: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1428

Experiments performed so far:
- Experiment A: Force a stream device sync after KV prefetch tasks; result: reduces backlog but increases median latency by ~7%.
- Experiment B: Reduce prefetch_concurrency to 2; result: decreases resident climb but throughput drops 12%.
- Experiment C: Turn off cudaMallocAsync (fallback to cudaMalloc); result: resident pages stable but CPU-side latency and overall cost increased significantly.
- Experiment D: Aggressively lower small-slab bin size from 32KB to 8KB to reduce internal fragmentation; result: mixed — reduced wasted memory but increased allocator ops and small CPU overhead.

Open hypotheses to validate:
- H1: Cross-stream references from KV prefetch kernels prevent immediate release; need cross-stream release pattern or stream-ordered deallocation.
- H2: Continuous-batching merge logic retains lightweight references to older KV caches until end-of-epoch; tightening lifetime can remove a large portion of churn.
- H3: cudaMallocAsync pool attributes (e.g., reuse thresholds / segment size) are suboptimal for high-mix seq workloads; tuning may reduce fragmentation without disabling async path.

Proposed next steps and trade-offs:
1) Implement a targeted experiment that records per-allocation "last-touch" stream and reference count to determine cross-stream retention (low-risk instrumentation, +1 day). Trade-off: extra metrics overhead.
2) Add optional path: stream-ordered free for KV prefetch buffers (cudaStreamAddCallback equivalent using event + pool release) as a toggleable runtime flag. Evaluate latency/regression (+3 days + can be behind a feature flag).
3) Add more granular pool attributes for small-slab bins and introduce on-demand compaction after a configurable deferred-free backlog threshold (complex change, testing-heavy, +1 sprint).
4) Short-term mitigation: auto-throttle prefetch_concurrency when allocator backlog > X (pinned metric). Quick to ship, but reduces prefetch effectiveness under load.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repro harness shows resident page growth limited to <5% over 8 hours for target workload mix with prefetch enabled.
- No regressions >5% in P50/P95 latency on PLG-style workload with prefetch-concurrency=4.
- New metrics surfaced in Grafana to alert when deferred-free queue exceeds threshold.

Notes on cross-team coordination:
- Console team: need a new dashboard tile for "deferred_free_backlog" and historic retention for 7 days (ticket created with PM).
- Research: validate quantization/kv-slice packing improvements from upcoming model-onboarding changes (may reduce KV memory footprint).
- SRE: recommend temporary scaling policy to provide burst headroom when backlog is detected to avoid customer-facing OOMs.
updates: 2026-03-01: Issue filed after on-call report of 2 customer-facing OOMs during overnight KV-heavy jobs. Initial triage by Aisha Patel (assignee).
2026-03-02: Collected nvprof/nsight traces and pushed repro harness (branch ENG-31500-repro). Added extended allocator counters (PR #1428).

2026-03-04: Ran Experiment A/B/C. Findings: stream sync reduces backlog but impacts latency; disabling cudaMallocAsync stabilizes memory but is not viable long-term due to cost. See profiling tarball.
2026-03-06: Design sync with Console and SRE — Console will add deferred_free_backlog panel; SRE will add temporary autoscaling policy when backlog spike detected.

2026-03-09: Implemented lightweight per-allocation 'last-touch stream' metadata in harness and replayed long-run tests. Early evidence supports H1 (cross-stream references present in ~30% of stale allocations).

2026-03-10: Decided to implement stream-ordered-release toggle behind feature flag and a small allocator compaction heuristic (deferred-free backlog threshold & aggressive on-threshold compaction). Planning 2-week spike to implement and measure. Assigned follow-ups and PR owners.
